meanings.note: aller + infinitive: tu vas l'agacer = you're going to annoy her
Je vais déjeuner. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').
Imperative used to encourage. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to go'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'allé').

examples.trans: I'm going to have lunch twice.

meanings.note: Feminine noun ('la arme', plural 'les armes') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'weapon'.

examples.text: Les personnages prennent les armes sans hésiter.
examples.trans: The characters take up arms without hesitating.

examples.text: Je ne te donnerai pas plus d'armes.
examples.trans: I will not give you more weapons.

meanings.note: je viens d'arriver = I've just arrived
Qu'est-ce qui arrive?. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to arrive'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'arrivé').

examples.text: Non, je viens d'arriver. Mon père, mais c'est compliqué.
examples.trans: No, I've just arrived. My dad, but it's complicated.

meanings.note: à + le contracted: au boulot, au téléphone

examples.trans: I've got a problem at work.

meanings.note: Core French preposition meaning 'with', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Et demain, tu déjeunes avec Audiard.
examples.trans: And tomorrow you're having lunch with Audiard.

meanings.note: determiner: ce soir = tonight, cette semaine = this week
pronoun: c'est = it is; tout ce que = all that

examples.text: Je ne peux pas venir ce soir.
Cette agence ne représente que des stars.
Magali, je dois voir la pièce de Koltès cette semaine.
examples.trans: Magali, I have to see the Koltès play this week.

meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Prefix 'com-' (from Latin 'cum') means 'with, together'. Core French verb meaning 'to understand'.

examples.text: Je comprends. C'est un coup dur.
examples.trans: I understand. It's a real blow.

meanings.note: J'étais dans les sous-vêtements. Core French preposition meaning 'in', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Dans une heure = in an hour. Core French preposition meaning 'in', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

examples.text: Tu connais beaucoup de monde dans le cinéma. Tu pourrais m'aider.
examples.trans: You know lots of people in film. You could help me.

meanings.note: Donner quelque chose à quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to give'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'donné').

examples.text: Fais du vélo! Ça donne des forces.
examples.trans: Ride a bike! It gives you energy.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le film', plural 'les films') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'film'.

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.
Tu as le film de Kechiche.
Vous tournez un film aux États-Unis?
examples.trans: Are you making a film in the United States?

meanings.note: Frapper quelqu'un. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hit'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'frappé').
Frapper à la porte. Regular first-group '-er' verb (from Latin first conjugation '-are') meaning 'to hit'; conjugates with 'avoir' in compound tenses (past participle 'frappé').

examples.text: Et ça n'explique pas pourquoi tu as frappé son assistante!
examples.trans: And that doesn't explain why you hit her assistant!

examples.text: C'est le destin qui frappe à ta porte.
examples.trans: It is destiny knocking at your door.

meanings.note: before the noun: une grande actrice = a great actress
Une grande star. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'big'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Descriptive French adjective meaning 'big'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Nous avons presque perdu une grande star!
examples.trans: We almost lost a big star!

meanings.note: J' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'I'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.text: Gabriel! Je suis à mon cours d'équitation.
examples.trans: Gabriel! I'm at my horse-riding lesson.

meanings.note: definite article; l' before a vowel

examples.text: C'est le prochain film de Tarantino.

meanings.note: Before the verb; m' before a vowel. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'me'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Mettre quelque chose dans. Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to put'.
Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to put'.

meanings.en: mettre en ordre = to put in order
meanings.note: Third-group irregular verb inherited from core Latin roots ('-ere'). Core French verb meaning 'to put'.

examples.text: Je l'ai mise dans une enveloppe.
examples.trans: I put it in an envelope.

examples.text: Il faut mettre nos comptes en ordre.
examples.trans: We need to put our books in order.

examples.text: J'ai pris la lettre. Je l'ai mise dans une enveloppe.
examples.trans: I took the letter. I put it in an envelope.

meanings.note: ne... pas = not; ne... rien = nothing; ne... que = only; n' before a vowel

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: at the end of a sentence: super, non?
Tag at the end of a question. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oh non! Je suis en retard.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'yes'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: second half of ne... pas; in speech ne is often dropped

examples.text: Tarantino ne prendra pas Cécile. Problème d'âge.
examples.trans: Tarantino won't take Cécile. A problem with her age.

meanings.note: Affectionate, a bit condescending. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'small'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.
Un petit cours. Descriptive French adjective meaning 'small'; agrees in gender and number with the noun it modifies.

examples.text: Oui, oui. J'ai juste besoin d'un petit cours.
examples.trans: Yes, yes. I just need a little lesson.

meanings.note: With ne: je n'en peux plus. Invariable French adverb meaning 'no more'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.
pronounced plys at the end of a sentence in this sense

examples.trans: I can't take any more, Andréa.

meanings.note: Feminine action/state noun from Latin '-tio'/'-sio'. Standard feminine noun meaning 'mental stress, psychological pressure'.

examples.trans: She undergoes a lot of pressure.

examples.text: Toute cette pression ne m'aide pas.
examples.trans: All this pressure does not help me.

examples.text: Ne te mets pas la pression, Sofia.
examples.trans: Do not put pressure on yourself, Sofia.

meanings.note: c'est moi qui... = I'm the one who...
Qui parle?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'who'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.

examples.trans: I'm the one who trained you!

examples.text: Tu ne pars pas. C'est moi qui te vire!
examples.trans: You're not leaving. I'm the one firing you!

meanings.note: On se reverra: we'll meet again. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 're-'/'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to see again'.
Literally 'until seeing again'. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Prefix 're-'/'ré-' marks repetition, return, or intensity. Core French verb meaning 'to see again'.

examples.trans: I want to see this film again.

meanings.en: part, role (in a film or play)
meanings.note: Un rôle dans un film. Masculine noun ('le rôle', plural 'les rôles') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'role'.

examples.text: Oui! Mon préféré, Pierre Niney, a un nouveau rôle.
examples.trans: Yes! My favourite, Pierre Niney, has a new part.

meanings.note: Masculine noun ('le sacrifice', plural 'les sacrifices') inherited through Romance vocabulary, used in everyday and professional French for 'sacrifice'.

examples.text: Ce métier demande parfois de grands sacrifices personnels.
examples.trans: This profession sometimes requires great personal sacrifices.

examples.text: Ses parents ont fait beaucoup de sacrifices pour ses études.
examples.trans: Her parents made many sacrifices for her studies.

meanings.note: Si tu veux = if you want. French conjunction meaning 'if', used to link clauses in spoken and written discourse.
answering a negative question: Aucune nouvelle? - Si!

examples.text: Si tu veux, on peut en parler demain matin.
examples.trans: If you want, we can talk about it tomorrow morning.

examples.text: Dis-moi tout de suite si le rôle t'intéresse.
examples.trans: Tell me right away if the role interests you.

meanings.note: Invariable French adverb meaning 'often'; placed immediately after the conjugated verb in simple tenses.

examples.text: C'est faux. Je suis souvent seule.

meanings.note: casual object pronoun, before the verb

examples.text: Je voulais te faire la surprise.
Je ne sais pas. Je voulais te faire la surprise.
examples.trans: I don't know. I wanted to surprise you.

meanings.note: Imperative: tiens! / tenez!. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to hold'.
Imperative: tiens! / tenez!. French '-ir' verb (from Latin '-ire'). Core French verb meaning 'to hold'.
Stressed form: et toi? = and you?. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'you'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
Informal, one owner; ton, ta, tes. Spoken French det expression meaning 'your', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: Tes premières vacances en huit ans!
examples.trans: Your first holiday in eight years!

meanings.note: takes a singular verb: tout le monde est là

examples.text: On est au Westin. Tout le monde est là.
examples.trans: We're at the Westin. Everyone is here.

meanings.note: one person you know well: friends, family, close colleagues

examples.text: Deux places pour mardi? Mardi, tu as le film de Kechiche.
examples.trans: Two tickets for Tuesday? On Tuesday you've got the Kechiche film.

meanings.note: indefinite article; des in the plural
Number; l'un = one of them. Spoken French det expression meaning 'a', common in natural conversation.

examples.text: L'un à midi, l'autre à deux heures.
examples.trans: One at noon, the other at two.

meanings.note: Place: à Paris, à mon cours. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Time: à midi. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.

meanings.en: au = à + le, aux = à + les
meanings.note: Contractions. Core French preposition meaning 'at', linking a noun phrase or infinitive complement to the clause.
Informal for cela. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
With time. High-frequency French pronoun meaning 'that'; clitic object forms precede the conjugated verb.
